glossary.title: Atlantis
glossary.description: An island civilization in Plato’s Timaeus and Critias, later reinterpreted by spiritual traditions and alternative researchers. This atlas compares those accounts without treating their chronologies as equivalent evidence.

glossary.title: Ancient civilizations
glossary.description: A starting point for exploring early settlements, ritual sites, and societies. “Civilization” has different meanings across the sources; each entry should explain the definition it uses.

glossary.title: Flood narratives
glossary.description: Stories about destructive waters appear in many traditions. Similar themes do not, on their own, establish a shared event or a common calendar date.

glossary.title: Göbekli Tepe
glossary.description: A Neolithic site in present-day Türkiye with monumental enclosures and carved pillars. Its UNESCO listing provides an archaeological chronology for the site.

glossary.title: Graham Hancock
glossary.description: Author of Fingerprints of the Gods, Magicians of the Gods, and America Before. The atlas indexes his official book synopses separately from archaeological site records; page-level print-edition research remains open.

glossary.title: Randall Carlson
glossary.description: A researcher followed by the project for catastrophe and ancient-landscape topics. The catalog includes a discovery record for Kosmographia episode 024; timestamp-level analysis is still pending.

glossary.title: Plato
glossary.description: The author of Timaeus and Critias. His dialogues provide the classical source for the Atlantis narrative. Stephanus numbers identify passages across editions.

glossary.title: The Bible
glossary.description: A collection of sacred texts interpreted through many religious and historical traditions. The atlas distinguishes what a passage says from dates assigned by later interpreters.

glossary.title: The Urantia Book
glossary.description: A spiritual text organized into numbered papers, sections, and paragraphs. Its narratives are presented as claims of the text, with passage-level references.

glossary.title: The Law of One
glossary.description: A body of channeled question-and-answer material also known as the Ra contact. Dates expressed as “years ago” are anchored to the session year before being placed on the atlas.

glossary.title: Neolithic
glossary.description: A regional archaeological term associated with changes in settlement, food production, and material culture. Its dates differ between places.

glossary.title: Buddhism
glossary.description: A research topic connecting Buddhist monuments, art, and the communities that used them.

glossary.title: Stonehenge
glossary.description: A monument built and altered in several phases. The earthwork and stone settings have distinct dated entries.

glossary.title: Cave art
glossary.description: Paintings and engravings preserved in caves. The age of an image and the date of its modern discovery are different events.

glossary.title: Dates, BP, and calendar years
glossary.description: BCE/CE dates, scientific BP ages, and a source’s “years ago” cannot be interchanged without a stated convention. The atlas records the basis of each conversion.

glossary.title: Ancient Egypt
glossary.description: Compare archaeological periodization with references to Egypt in classical, biblical, and alternative accounts.

glossary.title: Pyramids
glossary.description: A shape and architectural category used in different societies. Similar forms do not by themselves establish a shared origin.

glossary.title: Modern history
glossary.description: Documents and recorded milestones provide later reference points on the shared time scale.

glossary.title: Creation accounts
glossary.description: Narratives and philosophical accounts of origins. A cosmological story need not supply a calendar date.

glossary.title: Eden
glossary.description: The garden in Genesis and its reinterpretation in the Urantia Book. Each text has its own geography and chronology.

glossary.title: Human origins
glossary.description: A comparison topic for accounts of humanity’s beginnings, ancestry, and migrations. Source categories remain visible.

glossary.title: Nephilim
glossary.description: A term in Genesis 6:4 whose interpretation varies. The indexed entry links directly to the brief passage.

glossary.title: Babel
glossary.description: The city and tower in Genesis 11, associated in the narrative with dispersed languages and peoples.

glossary.title: Abraham / Abram
glossary.description: A central figure in Genesis. Related entries separate individual episodes and compare Melchizedek traditions.

glossary.title: Melchizedek
glossary.description: The king of Salem in Genesis 14 and a figure developed extensively in Urantia Paper 93.

glossary.title: Catastrophe narratives and hypotheses
glossary.description: A comparison topic for destructive floods, fires, and proposed ancient disasters. Shared themes and shared causes are separate questions.

glossary.title: Jesus
glossary.description: Compare canonical Gospel episodes with the additional narrative and explicit dates in the Urantia Book.

glossary.title: Nativity accounts
glossary.description: Accounts of Jesus’s birth and infancy. The texts vary in narrative detail and chronological specificity.

glossary.title: John the Baptist
glossary.description: A figure associated with baptism and the beginnings of Jesus’s ministry; Urantia also gives an infancy chronology.

glossary.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
glossary.description: The execution narrated in the Gospels and associated with later Christian cross symbolism.

glossary.title: Resurrection accounts
glossary.description: Narratives concerning Jesus after the crucifixion, indexed according to the text that presents them.

glossary.title: Pentecost in Acts
glossary.description: The gathering and arrival of the Spirit narrated in Acts 2, followed by an account of the early community.

glossary.title: Manuscripts and editions
glossary.description: A surviving manuscript’s production, its discovery, and a printed edition’s publication belong to separate timelines.

glossary.title: Mesopotamia
glossary.description: The Tigris–Euphrates region supplies geographical context for Sumer, Babel, and several flood interpretations.

glossary.title: Lemuria / Mu
glossary.description: Names used in alternative and channeled accounts of a proposed lost land. The Ra entries retain the dates and terminology of individual sessions.

glossary.title: Cycles of time
glossary.description: Recurring periods play different roles in philosophical and spiritual texts. Numerical cycles here are attributed to their sources.

glossary.title: Younger Dryas
glossary.description: A late-glacial climate interval that is also invoked in alternative catastrophe arguments. The existence of the interval and a proposed impact cause are distinct propositions.

glossary.title: Ignatius Donnelly
glossary.description: Author of Atlantis: The Antediluvian World. Its chapter-level entries document his arguments as an influential alternative interpretation.

glossary.title: Cosmology
glossary.description: Accounts of the universe’s origin and order, including Plato’s philosophical account and spiritual source traditions.

glossary.title: Indus region and Harappan cities
glossary.description: Explore Harappan urban sites alongside later cities in the wider Indus region. Taxila’s later settlements are not assigned to the Harappan civilization.

glossary.title: Water management
glossary.description: Reservoirs, canals, and related infrastructure offer a way to compare how settlements organized water access across different environments.

glossary.title: African kingdoms and urban centers
glossary.description: An index connecting Kush, Aksum, Mapungubwe, and other African political and urban histories. Each place keeps its own chronology.

glossary.title: Trade and exchange networks
glossary.description: Compare the movement of goods, people, and knowledge across linked cities and regions. A shared topic does not prove direct contact between two sites.

glossary.title: Christian traditions
glossary.description: A topic for Christian texts, communities, monuments, and material culture, connected with the separate Symbol Encyclopedia.

glossary.title: Sacred architecture and furnishings
glossary.description: A comparison category for built places of worship and the ritual objects described or used within them. Textual instructions and surviving buildings are different kinds of evidence.

glossary.title: Islamic learning and monuments
glossary.description: Explore the mosques, scholarly institutions, and urban contexts represented in the collection’s African site records.

glossary.title: Mississippian culture
glossary.description: The collection begins this regional topic with Cahokia’s settlements, earthworks, and ceremonial landscape.

glossary.title: Monumental earthworks
glossary.description: Large constructions formed by moving and shaping earth. Poverty Point and Cahokia provide distinct examples with different dates and cultural contexts.

glossary.title: Pueblo histories and places
glossary.description: Explore ancestral settlements and continuing Pueblo communities through Chaco, Mesa Verde, Taos, and related regional records.

glossary.title: Maya cities
glossary.description: Palenque, Tikal, and Copán provide entry points into Maya urban and monumental histories. Their individual site chronologies should not be collapsed into one rise-and-fall date.

glossary.title: Andean societies
glossary.description: A regional index connecting the distinct societies and landscapes represented by Tiwanaku, Chan Chan, and Nasca.

glossary.title: Geoglyphs
glossary.description: Large ground designs. The Nasca and Palpa entry records a particular landscape and date range rather than a universal explanation for such forms.

glossary.title: Exodus
glossary.description: The biblical narrative of departure from Egypt, wilderness travel, and covenant. Its relative sequence is indexed without imposing a disputed BCE chronology.

glossary.title: Moses
glossary.description: The central figure in Exodus’s accounts of deliverance, lawgiving, and sanctuary construction. Entries identify the individual episodes and their passages.

glossary.title: Passover in Exodus
glossary.description: Ritual instructions and a departure narrative in Exodus 12. The entry concerns this textual account; later practices need their own sources.

glossary.title: Sinai in Exodus
glossary.description: The mountain setting of encounter and covenant in Exodus. The atlas does not identify a modern archaeological location from the narrative alone.

glossary.title: Covenant in Exodus
glossary.description: The commitments, lawgiving, and renewals described in the Exodus passages indexed here.

glossary.title: Ark of the Covenant
glossary.description: The gold-covered chest specified in Exodus 25. Its description is a textual source, not a claim that the object has been archaeologically identified.

glossary.title: Ice-core chronology
glossary.description: Annual layers and marker horizons allow dated sequences to be compared. The GICC05 records use years before 2000 and retain maximum counting errors.

glossary.title: Ocean circulation and abrupt climate
glossary.description: A research topic linking freshwater routing, Atlantic circulation, and the climate evidence reviewed by NOAA.

glossary.title: Younger Dryas impact hypothesis
glossary.description: A proposed impact explanation for late-glacial changes. The indexed publications include an initial proposal, a critical review, and a bibliographically verified response; this selection is not a complete literature review.

glossary.title: Missoula megafloods
glossary.description: Repeated outburst floods from an ice-dammed lake, studied through regional sediments. Geological megaflood evidence does not itself establish a particular sacred flood narrative or Atlantis claim.
